answer: One agent, one marriage certificate: the civil registry signs each epoch challenge binding the agent's key to a single registered marriage, re-checked against the public register every epoch. A second key claiming the same certificate is rejected outright, since the registry, not the claimant, holds the record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real marriages — two real people, a ceremony and a fee of about $150 each, roughly $150,000, plus 1,000 spouses. A fable needs only words; a marriage needs two lives at the same wharf, and that shared record is the oasis no puppet farm can fake.
